title: The Node re-evaluation of L6's measured snapped tables and the exact arm
what: PREREGISTRATION.md Amendment 10 item 11 ("The Node re-evaluation"): after the decisive run, lexicon_core.js re-evaluates the 50 measured snapped tables, after traces on Rng(8000 + i) toy tables. It is reported, and it is needed before the browser shows L6 or L4(c) as holding (Common rules, "Authority"). L6 and L4(c) were decided by the Python reference; nothing here changes a decision.

readings.text: The exact arm is ranked from its committed text (the canonical H^3 lines of Amendment 1 item 6 for S): each line's four rationals are brought to one common denominator, the least common multiple of their denominators, and ranked as a lexicon_core.js Arm of kind lorentz. Its keys are positive multiples of rank.py's over 7^Lmax, so the order and the ties are the same; the text is also checked against this core's own pointExact lines.

A measured run's aps_sha hashes its .aps.json in the cache, which also holds the fractional-tie APs (A10.11), a quantity lexicon_core.js does not compute. That file is read only when its SHA-256 is the committed aps_sha; Node's closure and graph-edge APs are compared with it query by query, and the file is rebuilt from Node's two lists and its own two fractional lists, which must give aps_sha again. Without the file, the table's per-query APs are counted as not compared, never as equal.

The exact MAPs are compared as their p/q texts in lowest terms. The JSON keeps each text's SHA-256 (as LBENCH/1's closureMapSha and graphMapSha), its length and its binary64 value, and the texts themselves only where Node and the record differ.

The Lorentz keys are lexicon_core.js's exact kappa classes (SnapArm.keys); the reference ranked by the integer floor(a 2^(4K) / b), another image of the same order (tests/parity-lexicon.cjs checks that both give the same classes). The tie count is candidates minus distinct keys, summed over queries, in both.
